summary: 45-year-old man with recurrent discharge from an external opening 2 cm from the anal verge six months after a drained abscess; palpable cord to 7 o’clock. Simple low (Parks intersphincteric) fistula: fistulotomy. Not an anal fissure.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Discharge from a spot near the back passage
inputs.hpi: Perianal abscess drained 6 months ago. Since then a small opening beside the anus discharges pus and blood-stained fluid every few days, with intermittent discomfort that settles when it drains. No bowel symptoms, no weight loss. No IBD.

exam.other: Perianal: external opening 2 cm from the anal verge at 7 o’clock with granulation tissue; palpable cord towards the anal canal. DRE: normal tone, internal opening felt at the dentate line posteriorly. No abscess.

surgicalHistory: Incision and drainage of perianal abscess (6 months ago)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Fistula-in-ano — simple low intersphincteric
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Simple low intersphincteric fistula-in-ano (Parks) after a drained abscess. Fistulotomy.

mustInclude.note: ASCRS 2022: fistulotomy for simple fistulas with low risk of incontinence.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: getProtocolByIcd("K60.3") returns the anal_fissure protocol (prefix K60 covers fissure K60.0–K60.2 and fistula K60.3–K60.5); there is no fistula-in-ano protocol, and the perianal_abscess protocol (which has fistula steps) is keyed to K61.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a fistula-in-ano protocol keyed to K60.3–K60.5 (simple → fistulotomy; complex → MRI, loose seton, sphincter-preserving repair; Parks classification) and narrow anal_fissure to K60.0–K60.2.

mustExclude.note: A fistula-in-ano plan must not be an anal-fissure plan (chemical/surgical sphincterotomy).
mustExclude.knownGapNote: getProtocolByIcd("K60.3") returns the anal_fissure protocol (prefix K60 covers fissure K60.0–K60.2 and fistula K60.3–K60.5); there is no fistula-in-ano protocol, and the perianal_abscess protocol (which has fistula steps) is keyed to K61. The documented plan is GTN/diltiazem, botulinum toxin and lateral internal sphincterotomy.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano and rectovaginal fistula
guideline.section: Parks classification (Parks AG, Gordon PH, Hardcastle JD. Br J Surg 1976;63:1–12): inter-, trans-, supra-, extrasphincteric. Simple fistula-in-ano: fistulotomy; complex fistula: sphincter-preserving options; MRI/EUS for complex or recurrent disease
guideline.citation: Gaertner WB, Burgess PL, Davids JS, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of anorectal abscess, fistula-in-ano, and rectovaginal fistula. Dis Colon Rectum. 2022;65:964–985.

rationale: Base fistula case, confirmed diagnosis coded K60.3 (anal fistula). Checks that the protocol lookup returns a fistula plan: the K60 block contains fissures (K60.0–K60.2) and fistulas (K60.3–K60.5).
